schemes.exact: fixed-price, settles immediately. Upstream x402 itself supports substantially more network families than SITEBORNE's own launch-scoped subset (docs.x402.org/schemes/exact) — see SITEBORNE_SUPPORTED_X402_SCHEMES in src/network/schemes.ts for SITEBORNE's deliberate initial subset (eip155, solana), which is a product choice, not a spec limitation.
schemes.upto: usage-based (buyer authorizes a maximum, seller settles actual usage up to it), currently EVM-only (Permit2) upstream — this IS a real upstream constraint SITEBORNE mirrors exactly, not a SITEBORNE-specific narrowing (docs.x402.org/faq; getting-started/quickstart-for-sellers)
schemes.batch-settlement: off-chain vouchers settled in batches, not targeted by SUN-0700A

protocol.amount_representation: atomic-unit integer string, never binary floating point

extensions_referenced.payment-identifier: extensions['payment-identifier'], 16-128 char [a-zA-Z0-9_-]+, idempotency/retry protection — integrated in SUN-0700A checkpoint 2 via @x402/extensions/payment-identifier (see src/identifier/payment-identifier.ts)
extensions_referenced.bazaar: resource-server discovery metadata extension (key 'bazaar') — integrated in SUN-0700A checkpoint 4 via @x402/extensions/bazaar's declareDiscoveryExtension/validateDiscoveryExtension/validateDiscoveryExtensionSpec (see src/bazaar/discovery.ts, src/bazaar/validator.ts). Local declaration + local validation only — no facilitator catalog submission, no /discovery/resources query, no withBazaar()/listResources()/search() call anywhere in this package.
extensions_referenced.signed-offers-and-receipts: evaluated in SUN-0700A checkpoint 4 and deliberately deferred — see docs/decisions/0050-signed-offers-and-receipts-decision.md. Not implemented; the offer-receipt subpath is never imported (proven in src/tests/no-network.test.ts).

bazaar_extension.declaration_api: declareDiscoveryExtension(config): Record<'bazaar', DiscoveryExtension> — returns { bazaar: { info, schema } } keyed by BAZAAR.key ('bazaar')
explicitly_not_used: withBazaar (facilitator client extension — would query a live catalog)
bazaarResourceServerExtension (live server middleware hook — no live route exists yet)
known_shape_notes: declareDiscoveryExtension's public TS input type omits `method` (documented as normally filled in later by server-framework route enrichment) — this package supplies it directly since the real route/method is already known from the accepted OpenAPI source (src/bazaar/routes.ts); verified against the compiled implementation that it is accepted and used identically.

validateDiscoveryExtension rejects ANY $id/$ref in extension.schema not starting with '#' (hasExternalSchemaReference) — bundled input schemas must have their own top-level $id stripped before embedding (see schema-bundle.ts's stripDocumentIdentity), not just their inlined $refs.
bazaar_extension.upstream_maturity_note: the Bazaar extension is documented upstream as early/evolving (docs.x402.org/extensions/bazaar) — this baseline entry exists so x402:spec:verify can detect an incompatible future package/type change rather than silently drifting.

npm_packages_inspected.name: x402
npm_packages_inspected.reason: heavy transitive dependency surface (viem, wagmi, @solana/kit, wallet-standard packages) — inappropriate for a credential-independent, wallet-free protocol core

npm_packages_inspected.name: @coinbase/x402
npm_packages_inspected.reason: bundles @coinbase/cdp-sdk and viem — a facilitator/wallet SDK, not a pure protocol-core package

npm_packages_inspected.name: @x402/core
npm_packages_inspected.reason: pure protocol-core package (zod as its only dependency), exports V1/V2 Zod schemas, TS types, and Base64/JSON header codec primitives with no wallet/facilitator client — matches the SUN-0700A directive's 'no facilitator client belongs in the pure core' boundary
npm_packages_inspected.top_level_export: x402Version = 2 (this package's SUPPORTED_X402_VERSION is sourced directly from this constant)
known_gaps_verified_by_inspecting_dist: decodePaymentRequiredHeader/decodePaymentSignatureHeader/decodePaymentResponseHeader (from @x402/core/http) throw on invalid input rather than returning a closed result
those same decoders call JSON.parse with no size bound and no prototype-pollution guard
no exported Zod schema exists for SettleResponse (PAYMENT-RESPONSE payload) — only a plain TS type

@siteborne/protocol-x402's src/codec/headers.ts wraps the safe validating parsers (parsePaymentRequired/parsePaymentPayload) with its own bounded, pollution-safe decode step, and hand-maintains the one schema (SettleResponse) upstream does not export

npm_packages_inspected.name: @x402/extensions
npm_packages_inspected.reason: the parent @x402/extensions package bundles viem/jose/tweetnacl/siwe/@noble/curves/@scure/base for OTHER subpaths (sign-in-with-x, offer-receipt) — but the payment-identifier and bazaar subpaths' own compiled chunks import only ajv (+ @x402/core/server for bazaar), so both are safe to consume without pulling wallet/crypto code into this package's actual runtime. src/tests/no-network.test.ts statically asserts no other @x402/extensions subpath is ever imported (sign-in-with-x, offer-receipt, and builder-code remain explicitly excluded — see docs/decisions/0050-signed-offers-and-receipts-decision.md for why offer-receipt specifically was evaluated and deferred).

extensions_evaluated_but_not_used.reason_not_used: heavy signing-crypto dependency surface for both supported formats (EIP-712 needs a secp256k1 signer distinct from the payment wallet; JWS needs jose + did:web resolution/hosting) with no live facilitator, wallet, or deployed did:web document to actually exercise it against in this checkpoint — see ADR 0050's rubric for the full comparison.
